chunks.title: Hyphaema, hypopyon & blood in Schlemm's canal
chunks.tldr: Hyphaema: trauma, surgery, NVI, clotting problems/anticoagulants, HSV/VZV iritis, Fuchs, tumours (JXG, retinoblastoma). Hypopyon: infective keratitis, HLA-B27/Behçet uveitis, endophthalmitis, TASS, retained lens, FB, tumour (pseudohypopyon), rifampin/rifabutin.
points: Blood in Schlemm canal on gonioscopy: gonioprism pressure, Sturge–Weber, c-c fistula, SVC obstruction, hypotony.
Pseudohypopyon in a child → retinoblastoma.
Postop day 1 sterile hypopyon → think TASS.
chunks.hook: Hypopyon: Bugs, B27, Behçet, Bits of lens.

cards.q: Hypopyon within 24 h of cataract surgery, sterile, diffuse corneal oedema?

chunks.title: Corneal oedema, opacity in infants & big nerves
chunks.tldr: Infant cloudy cornea: 'STUMPED' — Sclerocornea, Tears in Descemet (forceps/glaucoma), Ulcer, Metabolic (MPS), Peters, Endothelial dystrophy (CHED/PPCD), Dermoid. Adult oedema: trauma, high IOP, hydrops, HSV, Fuchs, pseudophakic bullous, graft failure, ICE. Enlarged corneal nerves: MEN 2, NF, Acanthamoeba, keratoconus, leprosy.
points: Congenital oedema: birth trauma, congenital glaucoma, CHED (bilateral), PPCD.
Acquired also: chemical injury, CL overwear, uveitis, postoperative.
Big nerves also: Fuchs, failed graft, Refsum, Riley–Day, multiple myeloma, ichthyosis, normal variant.

cards.q: Enlarged corneal nerves + medullary thyroid carcinoma + phaeochromocytoma?
Name four causes of corneal opacity in infancy.
cards.a: Birth trauma, congenital glaucoma, Peters/sclerocornea, mucopolysaccharidosis (also CHED, PPCD, infection, dermoid).

chunks.title: Conjunctival signs
chunks.tldr: True membrane (bleeds when peeled): Strep, pneumococcus, diphtheria, HSV, chemical, ligneous. Pseudomembrane (peels easily): all above + adenovirus (EKC), gonococcus, chlamydia (newborn), pemphigoid. Pannus: CL hypoxia, staph, rosacea, HSV, trachoma, chemical, VKC. Symblepharon: pemphigoid, SJS, chemical.
points: Chemosis: allergy, inflammation, postop, venous congestion (c-c fistula), angioedema, myxoedema.
Dryness: exposure, Sjögren, vitamin A deficiency, pemphigoid, SJS, radiation.
Pigment: racial melanosis, PAM, naevus, melanoma, melanocytosis (episcleral blue-grey), Addison, adrenaline drops, mascara.
Dilated episcleral vessels without pain: uveal melanoma, c-c fistula, polycythaemia, leukaemia.
Verticillata: amiodarone, chloroquine, Fabry, phenothiazines, indomethacin, netarsudil/ripasudil.

cards.q: Difference between true membrane and pseudomembrane?
cards.a: True membranes are adherent and bleed when removed; pseudomembranes peel off easily without bleeding.

cards.q: New glaucoma drop class causing corneal verticillata?

chunks.title: Emboli & macular exudates
chunks.tldr: Emboli: cholesterol (Hollenhorst) = bright yellow at bifurcation → carotid. Platelet–fibrin = dull grey, long → carotid. Calcium = dull white near disc → heart valves. Talc = IV drug use. Cardiac myxoma: young, left eye. Fat/air → Purtscher-like.
points: Macular exudates common: diabetes, CNV, hypertension.
Less: macroaneurysm, Coats (children), capillary haemangioma, RVO, papilloedema, radiation.

cards.q: Dull white embolus on/near the optic disc points to which source?

chunks.title: Neovascularization, Roth spots & sheathing
chunks.tldr: Disc/posterior NV: diabetes, old CRVO/CRAO. Peripheral NV: sickle, BRVO, diabetes, sarcoid, OIS, pars planitis, ROP, FEVR, Eales, talc. Roth spots: diabetes, leukaemia, endocarditis, anaemia. Periphlebitis: syphilis, sarcoid, pars planitis, sickle, TB, MS, Behçet.
points: CNV: AMD, PCV, histoplasmosis, high myopia, angioid streaks, choroidal rupture; less: disc drusen, laser scars, VKH/MFC/serpiginous.
Choroidal folds: tumour, posterior scleritis, inflammation, hypotony, thyroid, hyperopia, papilloedema.
Optociliary shunts: meningioma, glioma, old CRVO, chronic papilloedema, glaucoma.
Normal fundus + poor vision: retrobulbar neuritis, toxic/LHON, amblyopia, early Stargardt, cone dystrophy, CAR/MAR, nonphysiologic.
Bull's eye: AMD, Stargardt, cone dystrophy, HCQ, albinism, Batten.
chunks.hook: Peripheral sea-fan NV = sickle (SC) until proven otherwise.

chunks.title: IOP high or low
chunks.tldr: Acute high IOP: angle closure, inflammatory OAG, malignant glaucoma, hyphaema, Posner–Schlossman, postop, suprachoroidal haemorrhage, c-c fistula, cleft closing, retrobulbar haemorrhage. Low IOP: ruptured globe, phthisis, RD/choroidal detachment, iritis, cyclodialysis cleft, wound leak, overfiltration.
points: Postop shallow AC + high IOP: pupil block, capsular block, suprachoroidal haemorrhage, malignant glaucoma.
Postop shallow AC + low IOP: wound leak, choroidal detachment, overfiltration.
Hypotony also: dehydration, ocular ischaemia, drugs, ciliary shutdown after trauma.

head: Shallow AC after surgery
Likely cause
rows: Pupil block, malignant glaucoma, suprachoroidal haemorrhage

chunks.hook: Flat chamber: hard eye = blocked/pushed; soft eye = leaking.

cards.q: Flat AC with low IOP after trabeculectomy — first test?
cards.a: Seidel test for a wound/bleb leak (also look for choroidal detachment).

chunks.title: Iris colour, lesions, NVI & lens signs
chunks.tldr: Lighter eye: congenital Horner, Fuchs, chronic uveitis, JXG, Waardenburg. Darker eye: melanocytosis, siderosis/retained FB, melanoma, ICE. NVI: diabetes, OIS, RVO/RAO, chronic RD, tumours. Anterior lenticonus = Alport.
points: Amelanotic iris lesions: amelanotic melanoma, granuloma (sarcoid, TB), JXG, medulloepithelioma, cyst.
Iridescent lens particles: drugs, hypocalcaemia, myotonic dystrophy, hypothyroidism.
Posterior lenticonus: idiopathic, PFV.
chunks.hook: Darker iris after an injury = iron inside.

cards.q: Heterochromia with the affected eye darker after trauma?
cards.a: Siderosis from retained iron foreign body.

chunks.title: RAPD, atrophy, paradoxical pupils & EOM thickening
chunks.tldr: Big RAPD: optic nerve disease, CRAO/CRVO, extensive RD. Small RAPD: amblyopia, dense VH, BRVO, smaller RD. Paradoxical pupils (dilate in light): CSNB, achromatopsia, ONH, LCA. Thick EOMs: thyroid (spares tendon) vs orbital inflammation (tendon involved).
points: Motility limited with proptosis → orbit (Ch 7); without → nerve palsies, myasthenia, CPEO, entrapment, Duane.
Optic atrophy: glaucoma, old CRAO/CRVO, AION, neuritis, papilloedema, compression, trauma; less syphilis, RP, toxic, LHON.
Isolated optic nerve mass: glioma (kids), meningioma (adults).
Infant nystagmus: congenital, spasmus nutans, cataract, aniridia, albinism, ONH, LCA, glioma.
chunks.hook: Thyroid spares the tendon; inflammation takes it.

cards.q: How do thyroid eye disease and orbital myositis differ on CT?
cards.a: Thyroid enlarges muscle bellies sparing tendons; idiopathic orbital inflammation involves the tendon.

cards.q: Paradoxical pupil constriction in darkness — name two causes.
cards.a: Congenital stationary night blindness, achromatopsia (also optic nerve hypoplasia, LCA).

chunks.title: Visual field patterns
chunks.tldr: Altitudinal: AION, optic neuritis, hemi-retinal occlusions. Arcuate: glaucoma. Bitemporal: chiasm (pituitary, meningioma, craniopharyngioma, aneurysm). Homonymous: behind chiasm (stroke/tumour). Big blind spot: papilloedema, drusen, MEWDS/AIBSE. Tunnel: glaucoma, RP, PRP, nonphysiologic.
points: Binasal: glaucoma, bitemporal retinal disease; rarely compression.
Central scotoma: macula, optic neuritis, compressive/toxic neuropathy.
Bitemporal mimic: tilted discs, nasal RP.
Tunnel also: CRAO with cilioretinal sparing, bilateral occipital infarcts with macular sparing, vit A deficiency, CAR/MAR.
chunks.hook: Respects horizontal = eye/nerve. Respects vertical = chiasm or brain.

chunks.title: Refraction changes & vitreous opacities
chunks.tldr: Hyperopic shift: orbital mass pressing globe, CSR, posterior scleritis, hypoglycaemia, presbyopia, post-RK. Myopic shift: pathologic myopia, diabetes (hyperglycaemia), nuclear cataract, keratoconus, miotics/sulfa drugs. Vitreous opacities: asteroid, blood, cells, snowballs, tumour, amyloid.
points: Sulfa drugs (topiramate) → acute myopia + angle closure.
Snowballs: pars planitis, sarcoid.
Rare vitreous: amyloid, Whipple disease.
